purpose_summary: XKey is a native macOS Vietnamese typing method (Telex, VNI, Simple Telex, auto-detect) that replaces unmaintained or incompatible Vietnamese IMEs on recent macOS (12+). It converts keystrokes into Vietnamese characters in any app. It adds productivity features: macros, quick typing, spell-check with personal dictionary, per-app smart switch, text conversion tools (case, code table, strip diacritics), and hotkey translation. It runs locally and collects no user data. This repo looks like a fork or personal checkout (git user LuffyTran) of the upstream xmannv/xkey project.
architecture_overview: Xcode project (XKey.xcodeproj, Swift, SwiftUI plus AppKit) with two runtime surfaces. (1) XKey: a menu-bar app that installs a CGEvent tap and injects replacement keystrokes or text into the focused app. It uses the Accessibility API and has special handling for app quirks (Spotlight, Raycast, terminals, browsers). (2) XKeyIM: an experimental Input Method Kit (IMKInputController) bundle installed in ~/Library/Input Methods, with a different bundle id (com.codetay.inputmethod.XKey). It gives flicker-free composition and shares the engine code. A third layer, Shared/, is compiled into both targets. It holds the input session and app-policy runtime (Shared/InputSession), AX helpers, app behavior detection, tap environment/event source, debug logging and translation languages. XKey/Core/Engine holds the Vietnamese engine (VNEngine, spell checker, ConvertTool, code tables). XKey/EventHandling holds the injection strategies. XKey/UI holds the SwiftUI settings, convert-tool and debug windows. XKey/Utilities and XKey/App (AppDelegate) cover lifecycle and helpers. Integrations: macOS Accessibility, Input Monitoring, Services menu, global hotkeys, App Group shared settings, online translation providers (Google, Tencent, Volcano), auto-update and Homebrew cask distribution, and a bundled GPL Vietnamese dictionary. Versioning lives in Version.xcconfig. build_release.sh packages releases. XKeyTests holds unit tests. The docs, plans and superpowers folders hold workflow and design notes, not runtime code.

critical_risks.issue: Fragile CGEvent injection and Accessibility behavior across macOS versions and apps
critical_risks.evidence: Recent commits are mostly per-app and focus fixes (secure input reminders, hotkey handling, Telegram Web rule). README says IM mode is better in Terminal/Spotlight. AdvancedInjectionMethods and AppBehaviorDetector exist for workarounds.
critical_risks.recommendation: Keep a per-app compatibility matrix with regression tests for the policy layer. Prefer the IMKit path where feasible. Test on each new macOS release.

critical_risks.issue: Privacy and security exposure of a keystroke-level tool
critical_risks.evidence: Needs Accessibility and Input Monitoring permissions, reads text via the AX API, handles secure input, and sends text to online translation providers (Google, Tencent, Volcano) despite the 'fully local, no data collection' claim.
critical_risks.recommendation: Document that translation sends text off-device. Exclude secure fields and password managers. Audit logging so DebugLogger never persists typed content. Keep the secret scan and dependency audit in CI.

critical_risks.issue: Test coverage is uncertain and likely thin for the event and UI layers
critical_risks.evidence: The heuristic found no obvious tests, but an XKeyTests directory exists. No CI config appears in the scanned index. Engine correctness is covered only if the tests actually target it.
critical_risks.recommendation: Confirm XKeyTests is wired into the scheme. Add engine golden tests (Telex/VNI tables, spell restore) and policy tests. Add CI running xcodebuild test.

critical_risks.issue: Two input paths share code, so changes can regress one path silently
critical_risks.evidence: Shared/ is compiled into XKey and XKeyIM. The XKeyIM README requires manually setting target membership on engine files. docs/superpowers has an XKeyIM event-tap plan.
critical_risks.recommendation: Move the shared engine into a Swift package or framework with its own tests. Verify both targets build in CI.

critical_risks.issue: Bundle id and App Group inconsistencies in docs
critical_risks.evidence: XKeyIM README lists the group as group.com.codetay.xkey in one place and group.com.codetay.inputmethod.XKey in setup steps. It also says to run `cd XKey` before build_release.sh, which looks stale.
critical_risks.recommendation: Verify the entitlements and Info.plist values, then correct the docs. A mismatch breaks settings sharing between the app and the IM.

critical_risks.issue: Release and signing process depends on private credentials and manual steps
critical_risks.evidence: The README documents Developer ID provisioning for XKeyIM. build_release.sh exists, and the app has auto-update and a Homebrew cask.
critical_risks.recommendation: Script notarization and update-feed publishing. Keep credentials in the keychain or environment variables, never in the repo.

critical_risks.issue: Licensing mix: MIT project with a GPL Vietnamese dictionary
critical_risks.evidence: The README badge says MIT. The spell-check feature notes a ~200KB dictionary under a GPL license.
critical_risks.recommendation: Check that the dictionary's license is compatible with distribution or is kept as a separate data file. Document attribution.

critical_risks.issue: Working tree has uncommitted workflow artifacts
critical_risks.evidence: git status shows a modified .gitignore plus untracked docs/project-context.md, docs/sharded/ and plans/.
critical_risks.recommendation: Decide whether the AI workflow artifacts belong in the repo. Ignore them or commit them deliberately.
